content: 1. Products containing multivalent cations, such as calcium, magnesium, or aluminum, can impair the gastrointestinal absorption of tetracyclines, potentially reducing their therapeutic efficacy. To mitigate this interaction, administer tetracyclines separately from these products. 2. Sarecycline can increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of drugs that are substrates of the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter, such as sofosbuvir, tacrolimus, temsirolimus, teniposide, tenofovir (AF and DF), testosterone, tolvaptan, topotecan, trabectedin, velpatasvir, vemurafenib, venetoclax, verapamil, vinblastine, vincristine (including liposomal formulations), voxilaprevir, abemaciclib, aliskiren, apixaban, betrixaban, brentuximab vedotin, budesonide, and carfilzomib. Use caution and monitor for toxicities associated with these P-gp substrates, as dose adjustments may be necessary when co-administered with sarecycline. 3. Sarecycline may decrease the absorption and efficacy of certain drugs, such as amoxicillin and ampicillin, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative therapies, as tetracyclines can interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 4. Sarecycline may increase the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative therapies and monitor closely. 5. Products containing multivalent cations, such as trimagnesium citrate anhydrous, tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate, aluminum hydroxide, magnesium carbonate, magnesium trisilicate, calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, calcium/vitamin D, carbonyl iron, bismuth subgallate, and bismuth subsalicylate, can reduce the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely, and separate the administration of tetracyclines and these products. 6. Concomitant use of oral retinoids, such as acitretin or bexarotene, with tetracyclines, including sarecycline, may increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (intracranial hypertension). Avoid or use alternative therapies, and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 7. Zinc can decrease the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline by binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely, and separate the administration of oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts by at least 2 hours. 8. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 9. Sarecycline may increase the toxicity of certain drugs, such as bendamustine, by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor for toxicities, as dose adjustments may be required. 10. Sarecycline may increase the toxicity of certain drugs, such as aliskiren, by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor for toxicities, as dose adjustments may be required.
